chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Sirran, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked him: How many women were made permissible for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?
He said: 'As many as He willed, of any number.'
I said: Inform me about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And a believing woman if she dedicates herself to the Prophet'
The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And a believing woman if she dedicates herself to the Prophet'
He said: 'The gift (of oneself) is not permissible except for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). As for others, marriage is not valid for them except with a dowry.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Prophet's marriage and others' regarding dowry and self-dedication?
ai.summary: Zurarah queries Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the Prophet’s unique exemption from the standard dowry requirement, citing the verse in Surah Al-Ahzab. The Imam clarifies that while the Prophet could accept a woman’s self-dedication (hibah) without a formal mahr, this privilege was exclusive to him; for all other men, a valid marriage contract necessitates a specified dowry. This distinction highlights the theological principle of the Prophet’s special status (khass) in marital regulations as understood in Shia jurisprudence.
